subject: SLO alignment + benchmark/harness roadmap for Marley Retail
messages:
From: Daniel Park <dpark@marleyretail.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 29 Mar 2027 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Alignment on performance SLOs & benchmark plan

Connor / team — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap from our side and a few asks so we can get the qualification moving: 

Summary of what we need to validate:
- Primary SLOs we expect to qualify against: p95 latency <= 120 ms (inference-only), p99 < 300 ms for typical prompts (~250 tokens).
- Sustained throughput target: 150–200 RPS for long-tail peak windows.
- Concurrency target: 40 concurrent sessions with KV cache behavior (session affinity).
- Streaming requirement: partial token streaming (server-driven chunking) to our web clients with <= 50 ms inter-chunk delay.

What we discussed we need from Redwood to reproduce results:
1) The exact prompt set you will run (we shared an anonymized workload earlier; happy to use Redwood's canonical prompt pack).
2) Measurement definitions: how p95/p99 are computed (per-request vs per-token), tokenization details, warm vs cold cache handling.
3) Eval harness: can you provide a containerized harness or a reproducible script (we prefer Docker/K8s manifest) so we can re-run tests?
4) Attachments: I attached a short workload summary and our baseline client qps profile.

Next steps proposal from Marley: we can provision a test subnet and service account for Redwood to run a first-pass harness (or accept Redwood-run results if we get the harness). Can you map owners and a timeline (ideally first-pass within 7 business days)?

Thanks — looking forward to the prompt set + measurement spec.

—Daniel
Director, Engineering
Marley Retail
[Attachment: workload_summary.xlsx (18 KB)]

From: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.ai>
To: Daniel Park <dpark@marleyretail.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 29 Mar 2027 16:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Alignment on performance SLOs & benchmark plan

Daniel — thanks for the clear recap and for sharing the workload summary. Team copied for visibility. Below are clarifications and a concrete roadmap we can start executing on Monday: 

Clarifications / measurement definition (short):
- Latency windows: we will report p50/p95/p99 on a per-request basis where request = single generate call (this includes model forward + token streaming time). For long responses we will also report tokenized per-second throughput and average per-token latency.
- Tokenization: we will use the same BPE tokenizer as the model variant we onboard (we'll include tokenizer version in the spec).
- Warm vs cold: baseline will be "warm" with an initial priming phase (2k requests); we'll also run a cold-start sweep (100 cold requests) to show delta.
- Streaming: we'll measure TTF (time-to-first-token) and inter-chunk latency; inter-chunk windows will be reported as median and 95th percentile.

Proposed owners & timeline:
- Marissa Cole (marissa@redwood.ai): onboard prompt_set_v1 and run initial harness against Redwood-hosted dedicated instance; produce raw metrics and trace evidence (7 business days).
- Lauren Bishop (lauren@redwood.ai): validate infra config (model variant, quantization profile, batching policy) and confirm reproduce config for a containerized harness.
- Connor O'Brien (connor@redwood.ai): coordinate network/test accounts and provide measurement_spec_v1.md + prompt_set_v1.json.

Deliverables we will attach in the next message (expected today):
- prompt_set_v1.json (anonymized prompts + metadata)
- measurement_spec_v1.md (exact metric definitions, client harness commands, and seed RNGs for deterministic eval)
- optional: Dockerfile + harness run script stub (we'll push this to the shared Drive link).

Notes / tradeoffs to surface now:
- Sustained 200 RPS at p95 <= 120 ms depends heavily on model size and quantization; we'll include suggested model variants with perf profiles. If Marley prefers smaller quantized variants we can hit higher throughput but must validate quality.
- Streaming inter-chunk delay is influenced by batching policy; to meet <= 50 ms we may recommend asynchronous flush thresholds (we'll include recommended policy).

Action: we'll upload the artifacts and a proposed run schedule to the shared Drive by EOD PST. If you want it run inside your subnet, Marissa will need the service account + minimal IAM bits to spin the harness.

Connor
Sr. Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
connor@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0182
[Attachment: prompt_set_v1.json (2.1 KB), measurement_spec_v1.md (4.6 KB)]

From: Daniel Park <dpark@marleyretail.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 29 Mar 2027 18:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Alignment on performance SLOs & benchmark plan

Appreciate the fast follow, Connor. Two quick items: 
1) We prefer Redwood to run the first pass (faster for us) and then we'll run the harness in our subnet for verification. Please proceed with Redwood-hosted run if that's fine.
2) For reproducibility we'd like a Docker image / manifest so our infra folks can replay. Can you confirm the harness will be deterministic (seeded RNGs, pinned tokenizers) and provide version pins for model + runtime?

If you can upload the artifacts to the Drive and ping our infra slack channel (#marley-infra), we'll kick off review. Also confirm if we need an interim NDA amendment for access to our prod-like subnet.

Thanks — Daniel
